newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Reid buys South Port businesses.
newsitem.headline: Reid buys South Port businesses.

text.p: Reid Farmers said on Friday negotiations for acquiring rural businesses from South Port's subsidiary company, Southland Farmers Ltd, had been successfully concluded.
Reid said the price to be paid was variable, depending upon the level of seasonal finance and trade debtor balances at the date of settlement, but was expected to be in the region of NZ$10.5 million.
The businesses to be acquired by Reid consist of the livestock trading, merchandise trading, wool broking, real estate and finance businesses.
"The acquisition of Southland Farmers rural businesses extends Reid Farmers' existing operations in Southland and reinforces Reid Farmers' long term commitment to the rural sector," the company said.
The purchase was unconditional from Friday, with settlement planned for the June 3.
The purchase would be settled in cash and was to be funded from increased credit lines and existing resources within the Reid Farmers Group.
South Port New Zealand would use the funds to strengthen its overall equity position.
